chunks.text: What if a demo video was not a recording you capture, but a value you compile? This is DemoCreate.
One declarative artifact describes a codebase or research paper and compiles into frames, captions and video. Its provenance records are unsigned, not authentication.

scenes.title: A demo is a value, not a recording

chunks.text: A demo is a declarative spine: scenes of narration chunks, each an ordered stream of typed actions. Three ideas carry the whole system.

bullets: Core defaults reproduce bytes for the same artifact, assets, configuration and environment.
Optional adapters load on demand; default narration is silent, not an automatically installed neural voice.
Measured WAV durations set clip windows; word positions remain character-weighted estimates.

chunks.text: The spine is plain data: scenes contain narration chunks and typed actions. Synthesis records audio paths and measured timing in the resolved output artifact.

Interfaces separate the core defaults from optional adapters. Silent narration uses the standard library; a system voice needs a usable speech binary. This canonical recipe selects locally provisioned Kokoro.
Clip duration is measured. Word timing is estimated: the default transcriber spreads known text across the clip by character length. It does not detect spoken word onsets.

params.code:
clips = synthesize_demo(demo, ws)
sync_demo(demo, clips)        # duration-based word estimates
for action in chunk.actions:
    action.timestamp_ms = word_time(action.trigger_word)
# every frame is held for its measured clip

scenes.title: What you are seeing, right now

chunks.text: Everything you are watching is generated from that spine. The code you just saw typed itself in. Look at this frame.

bullets: The canonical recipe selects Kokoro with local model files; the default backend remains silent.
The waveform samples assembled audio at output-frame times.
Backgrounds start fitted to the viewport; camera zoom and overlays can crop or obscure content.

chunks.text: YAML configuration selects themes, layout, resolution presets including four K, and encoding controls. Actual quality depends on input detail and encoding settings.
PDF text extraction uses poppler system binaries. Abstract, section and caption detection are heuristic. Figure backgrounds need locally available images.
A portfolio pass describes repository folders from README files and Python definitions. It attempts one video per selected project and reports failures, rather than inventing unsupported details.

bullets: Portfolio reads available README text, Python definitions and bounded repository statistics.
Selection and extraction do not use a language model; voiced video still needs working TTS and ffmpeg.
This showcase is hand authored; portfolio shares its rendering and export pipeline.

chunks.text: Eight subsystems share a declarative spine. Narration, rendering and export also depend on configuration, assets and the selected runtime environment.
Engineering gates check the core with real files and a coverage threshold. Eight subsystems, five themes, four K presets, and no external media executables for the core build.
Renders carry attribution three ways. These records are unsigned: they associate content, but do not authenticate an author or video.

bullets: On-screen metadata bars — author, source, a running clock.
Container tags in the MP4, readable by any player or ffprobe.
An unsigned poster payload checks a Demo digest; it does not authenticate cover pixels, video bytes or authorship.

chunks.text: Rendering and basic verification check stream shape, audio energy and sampled picture variance. These checks do not establish intelligibility or acoustic word alignment.

params.output: Illustrative output — not executed by DemoCreate: verification summary

chunks.text: Declarative. Deterministic. Dogfooded. This entire video was compiled by DemoCreate from one file. Edit it, re-render, and never record a take again.
